name_reason: Already compliant: data_fd2_battle_* convention, descriptor reflects role (post-action consequence index) and data type (idx = scalar index), no Ghidra address residue. Matches its paired sibling table data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table; renaming would force renaming the table and ripple across many call sites with no semantic gain. 'consequence' is a reasonable label for what btltab.c documents as chapter-event handlers dispatched as the action's after-effect.
purpose: Pending post-action consequence selector: index into the 90-entry data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table (chapter-event handler dispatch table), or 0xFF for 'none'.
logic_summary: Reset to 0xFF before each actor finishes an action. fd2_check_tile_event_post_action (btl_turn.c) stores the event record's consequence byte (*(rec+0x33)) here when the actor lands on a matching event tile (gated by event_type == expected_event_type). After the action, callers (fd2_game_main_loop, fd2_field_command_menu_loop, fd2_player_action_menu_loop, fd2_npc_turn_phase_team1, fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0) test it: if != 0xFF they tail-call data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table[idx](char_idx), then reset it to 0xFF. Stored as a full dword though the value is an 8-bit id (MOVZX from a byte).
element_semantics: Single scalar: an 8-bit consequence/event id (0x00..0x59 valid) stored in a 32-bit slot; 0xFF = sentinel 'no pending consequence'. Indexes data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table (90 function pointers).
comment_original_issue: Original parenthetical described the indexed handlers as 'counter-attack / death / status proc', which is inaccurate: btltab.c documents the indexed table as the chapter-event handler table (fd2_chapter_event_handler_NN__*). Also did not name the writer (fd2_check_tile_event_post_action) nor note the value is an 8-bit id stored in a dword.
notes: Verified width via disasm at 0x13a95: MOV dword ptr [0x00051a8f],EDX with EDX = MOVZX byte ptr [EAX+0x33] (consequence_idx from event record). read_memory shows ff000000 (LE) = 0xFF initial. Ghidra data plate was empty (null); created concise plate from src conclusion and saved program. Stale compile warnings from prior scripts in run_script_inline output are unrelated noise; my scripts emitted SET_OK / SYM / DATA correctly.
